propositions: Directory creation and first event file write to ticket directories occur in a non-atomic window (mkdir outside lock, os.replace inside lock), leaving orphaned empty directories if the process is interrupted between these operations
Orphaned ticket directories are flagged by fsck as both MISSING_CREATE and FOREIGN_STORE_PATH, matching the signature found in production (8 stray dirs under illsuited-erect-ibis)

New staging.py module creates directory and first event atomically in a temporary dot-prefixed staging path, then publishes both with a single os.rename under the write lock, making the directory invisible to fsck scanners until fully created

Both single-event (stage_and_commit) and batch (batch_stage_and_commit) code paths, plus reconciler inbound_translate and dispatch_one BRIDGE_ALERT emission, share the same mkdir-then-first-file vulnerability and are converted to use StagedEvent.promote

Sweep of stale .tmp-newticket-* staging directories removes only writer-owned staging paths whose processes are provably dead (via v2 pid-namespace stamp), respecting the 043f boundary that rejects writer-side cleanup of ticket directories themselves
No event format or committed worktree layout changes; renamed event bytes still derive from the single canonical serializer and go through the same lock discipline
